messages:
alice_sales: Hey team — Acme demo stalled. Customer hits a 413 when sending their 1.2MB context bundle to our /v1/generate endpoint via their proxy. Need quick unblock for this afternoon demo.
mark_se: Ugh. Do we have the exact error from the gateway? 413 usually means body too large at proxy/nginx, or our API gateway limit. Any logs?
tina_ml: Also ask if payload is UTF-8 JSON or base64. Base64 can add ~33% bloat, UTF-16 doubles.
alice_sales: They said it's JSON UTF-8, but the client is embedding a 400k CSV and a full conversation history — packaged as one field. Gateway response: "413 Request Entity Too Large" from customer side (Azure APIM).
jane_se: Two quick options: 1) presign direct upload + reference URL in request (we already recommend for large attachments), or 2) chunk the context on client and stream incremental context to us. Which can they do?
alice_sales: Customer firewall blocks outbound S3 presign endpoints, so presign flow is blocked. They can implement client-side chunking but want guidance/examples and worry about reassembly & token counting.
mark_se: For chunking: split into logical chunks <= ~200k bytes, compute approximate tokens per chunk (1 token ~= 4 chars for English), then send as multiple messages with a final "assemble" call or stream. If they use streaming, we can accept multiple parts and append in-order.
tina_ml: Important: advise gzipping before upload. gzip typically reduces CSV heavy payloads massively. If they gzip client-side, set header Content-Encoding: gzip and our gateway accepts it. Example curl: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/upload" \\
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\
  --data-binary @payload.gz
```
But the customer's APIM might still count compressed size against limit — depends on proxy.
sam_support: If APIM is the choke point, ask customer to increase the max body size there. For Azure APIM -> 'set <gateway> request-size-limit' or change the policy. We can share exact docs.
alice_sales: They don't want to change infra for a POC. Any short-term hacks?
jane_se: Workaround: host a small temporary private ingest on our Dedicated trial or use our streaming websocket endpoint which keeps request bodies small and sends tokens incrementally. Websocket approach often bypasses APIM single-body limits. Sam, can we enable a trial streaming token for them?
sam_support: Yes, I can spin up a short-lived streaming token and forward connection info. Need customer IP allowlist (they're behind a corporate NAT).
mark_se: Also watch out for token counting vs bytes — when reassembling, we enforce model context window. Recommend they drop non-essential metadata and compress the CSV to embeddings instead of raw text if they need semantic search, that reduces context size a lot.
alice_sales: Pricing question: customer asked if large-context usage costs more. Answer?
jane_se: We bill by input + output tokens. Large context increases token count (and cost). Suggest sending compressed/embedded summaries to reduce costs; we can estimate tokens from bytes to give a SKU estimate.
ops_bot: deploy-bot: created support ticket #SUP-3421 for streaming trial token (assigned to sam_support).
alice_sales: Great — I'll tell them we can offer a streaming/demo token and send chunking examples + gzip note. Sam, can you cc me on the trial details?
sam_support: Will do, spinning up token now. ETA 20m.
tina_ml: I'll drop a short example python snippet for client-side chunking and token estimate in the support ticket.
jane_se: Also adding escalation: if they need unlimited single-request size we can propose Dedicated with a custom gateway; I can draft pricing addendum if they escalate.
alice_sales: Thanks all — keeping this thread for the next demo sync. :thumbsup:
